chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said:

I witnessed Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) while he was being carried around the Kaaba in a litter, and he was severely ill. So whenever he reached the Yemeni Corner, he would order them, and they would place him on the ground. Then he would extend his hand from the opening of the litter until he dragged it on the ground, then he would say: 'Raise me.'
So when he did that repeatedly in each circuit, I said to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you, O son of the Messenger of Allah! Indeed, this is difficult for you.'
So he said: 'I heard Allah, Mighty and Majestic, saying: 'That they may witness benefits for them'.'
So I said: 'Benefits of the world or benefits of the Hereafter?' So he said: 'All.'

key_terms.الرُّكْنُ الْيَمَانِيُّ: The Yemeni Corner of the Kaaba
key_terms.مَحْمِلٌ: Litter or carriage for carrying a person

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and spiritual significance of a sick person performing Tawaf while being carried?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) physical devotion during his final illness, emphasizing the tactile connection with the Kaaba as a means of spiritual and worldly benefit. By citing the verse 'That they may witness benefits for them' (22:28), he clarifies that the ritual encompasses both material and spiritual gains, a point of scholarly discussion regarding the holistic nature of Hajj rituals. The act of dragging his hand on the ground at the Yemeni Corner underscores the importance of humility and physical engagement even in weakness.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Al Fyzayl, from Al Rabie Bin Khushaym who said, ‘

I witnessed Abu Abdullahasws, and heasws was being performed Tawaaf with around the Kaaba in a carriage, and heasws was extremely ill. So it was such that every time heasws reached the (Yamani) corner, heasws ordered them, so they placed himasws by the ground. Then heasws extracted hisasws hand out from the opening of the carriage until heasws dragged it upon the ground, then heasws was saying: ‘Raise measws’.

So when he<sup>asws</sup> did that repeatedly during each circuit, I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>, O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! This is difficult upon you<sup>asws</sup>’.
So heasws said: ‘Iasws heard Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic saying [22:28] That they may witness benefits for them’.
So I said, ‘Benefits of the world or benefits of the Hereafter?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘All’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from al-Rabi‘ ibn Khuthaym who has said the following:

“I saw abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, being carried for Tawaf around al-Ka‘bah in a carriage and he was seriously ill. Whenever he would reach al-Yemaniy corner he commanded to place him on the ground, and he would extend his hand from the carriage and pull it on the ground then say, ’Lift me up.’
When he did so many times in every turn of walking around the House, I said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, O child of the Messenger of Allah, this is difficult for you.’
He (the Imam) said, T heard Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, say, . . so that they witness the benefits for them.’” [22:28]
I then asked, ‘Is it worldly benefits or the hereafter?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘It is the benefits of both of them.’”
